UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores core profile information for a user in the InsightFlow application, excluding authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. (Primary Key)

email.description: The user's email address, primarily for display and identification. Not used for authentication.

role.description: The user's role within the application, e.g., 'standard', 'admin'.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

lastSeen.description: Timestamp of the user's last activity or login.

defaultModeId.description: Reference to the default Mode entity for this user. (Relationship: Mode 1:N UserProfile)

UserPreference.title: UserPreference
UserPreference.description: Stores user-specific display and interaction preferences, including visual settings and schema versioning for migrations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserPreference entity. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity this preference belongs to. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N UserPreference)

schemaVersion.description: Version of the user preference schema, used for migration logic during updates.

density.description: Preference for UI element density, e.g., 'compact', 'standard'.

motion.description: Preference for UI animations and motion, e.g., 'full', 'reduced'.

contrast.description: Preference for UI contrast levels, e.g., 'standard', 'high'.

fontScaling.description: Scaling factor for fonts in the UI, e.g., 1.0, 1.2.

UserLayout.title: UserLayout
UserLayout.description: Defines a user's personalized dashboard layout for a specific mode, including panel configurations and grid settings.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserLayout entity. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity this layout belongs to. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N UserLayout)

schemaVersion.description: Version of the layout schema, used for migration logic during updates.

modeId.description: Reference to the Mode entity this layout is associated with. (Relationship: Mode 1:N UserLayout)

lastMigratedAt.description: Timestamp of the last time this layout's schema was migrated.

gridConfigurationJson.description: JSON string representing the grid layout configuration for panels within this layout.

PanelConfiguration.title: PanelConfiguration
PanelConfiguration.description: Defines the specific settings for a single panel within a user's dashboard layout.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PanelConfiguration entity. (Primary Key)

userLayoutId.description: Reference to the UserLayout entity this panel configuration belongs to. (Relationship: UserLayout 1:N PanelConfiguration)

stableIdentifier.description: A stable, programmatic ID for the panel, used for consistent referencing across layout updates (e.g., 'primary_chart_01').

detailsJson.description: JSON string containing detailed configuration specific to the panel's type (e.g., symbol for a chart, feed source for news).

Mode.title: Mode
Mode.description: Defines the application's pre-configured display modes (e.g., Focus Mode, Minimal Mode, Pro Desk Mode) and their default characteristics.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Mode entity. (Primary Key)

name.description: The display name of the mode, e.g., 'Focus Mode'.

description.description: A brief explanation of the mode's purpose and features.

maxCharts.description: The maximum number of charts allowed in layouts for this mode.

guidedOverlayEnabled.description: Indicates if a guided overlay should be enabled by default for this mode.

reducedMotion.description: Indicates if reduced motion settings are preferred for this mode.

reducedVisualNoise.description: Indicates if visual noise should be reduced by default for this mode.

defaultOrder.description: The default order in which this mode should appear in lists, used for steering users.

ExperimentAssignment.title: ExperimentAssignment
ExperimentAssignment.description: Records a user's assignment to an A/B test or experiment variant.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ExperimentAssignment entity. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity assigned to this experiment. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ExperimentAssignment)

experimentName.description: The name or identifier of the experiment.

assignmentVariant.description: The specific variant (e.g., 'control', 'variant_A') assigned to the user.

assignedAt.description: Timestamp when the user was assigned to this experiment variant.

Feedback.title: Feedback
Feedback.description: Stores user-submitted feedback, issues, 'confusion points', or structured reports.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Feedback entity. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity who provided the feedback. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Feedback)

message.description: The detailed message or description of the feedback.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the feedback was submitted.

contextJson.description: Optional JSON string representing the application context or UI state when feedback was provided.

UserEvent.title: UserEvent
UserEvent.description: Logs significant user interactions or application events for analytics and tracking purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserEvent entity. (Primary Key)

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity associated with this event. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N UserEvent)

eventType.description: The category or type of event, e.g., 'onboarding_complete', 'mode_selected', 'dashboard_viewed'.

eventDetailsJson.description: Optional JSON string containing additional details specific to the event (e.g., selected mode ID, panel interacted with).

params.name: layoutId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent user layout.

params.name: panelConfigurationId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific panel configuration.

params.name: eventId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific user event.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for InsightFlow prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** The design primarily achieves authorization independence by leveraging path-based ownership for all user-specific data. Every user's personal data (profile, preferences, layouts, experiment assignments, feedback, and events) is stored under a root collection `/users/{userId}/...`. The `{userId}` wildcard in the path *must* directly match `request.auth.uid` from Firebase Authentication. This means that security rules can authorize access to these documents by simply checking `request.auth.uid == userId` (where `userId` is the path segment), without needing any `get()` operations to fetch parent documents or external authorization contexts. For example, a user's preferences at `/users/{userId}/preferences/{preferenceId}` are authorized directly by the `{userId}` in the path. This eliminates complex hierarchical authorization dependencies, making rules atomic, robust, and easy to debug. 

For global roles (e.g., an 'admin' role that allows access to all feedback), the `role` field within the `UserProfile` document (`/users/{userId}`) is used. While the strictest interpretation of 'Authorization Independence' might forbid *any* `get()` call, a single `get()` to retrieve the requesting user's *own* `UserProfile` (`get(/users/$(request.auth.uid))`) for a global role check is considered an acceptable, controlled exception. This is because it queries a property of the *principal* (the authenticated user) rather than a hierarchical dependency of the *resource* being accessed. This approach respects DBAC (Database Access Control) without relying on Firebase Custom Claims.

**Clarity of Intent (Debuggability) and Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**

1.  **Private User Data:** All personal and user-specific configurations are segregated under `/users/{userId}`. This includes subcollections for `/preferences`, `/layouts`, `/experimentAssignments`, `/feedback`, and `/userEvents`. All documents within these subcollections inherently share the same ownership-based security posture (`request.auth.uid == userId`), making rules simple (e.g., `allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId;`). This ensures no mixing of data with different access requirements.
2.  **Global Read-Only Data:** Application-wide configurations, such as the predefined `Mode` entities, are stored in a top-level collection `/modes/{modeId}`. These documents are public and read-only for all authenticated users, allowing for straightforward rules like `allow read: if request.auth.uid != null;`.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** By enforcing strict path-based ownership for user data and segregating global data, the structure inherently supports Queryable Authorization Patterns (QAPs). Queries on `/users/{userId}/layouts` will only return layouts owned by `request.auth.uid` because the rules will only allow access to that specific path. Similarly, listing all available `modes` (`/modes`) is a simple authorized public read. There is no need for complex `where` clauses in security rules that attempt to filter data, as the data's location already defines its access context.

**Invariants and Predictable Schema:** The structure uses descriptive wildcards (e.g., `{userId}`, `{layoutId}`) and mandates `schemaVersion` and `lastMigratedAt` fields within `UserPreference` and `UserLayout` to manage schema evolution. Denormalization is achieved by having `userId` explicitly in all relevant paths for user-owned data, making ownership explicit and rule evaluation independent.

**App Requirements Alignment:** The structure explicitly supports the 'Correct Build' spec, including versioned personalization schemas and clear segregation of user-specific data. It also allows for granular control over user preferences and layout configurations required by the dynamic dashboards and UI modes features.
